OE_T1_Better_Worse: Having the client request, manager approval, and automated staff notification all in one system was much cleaner and less error-prone than juggling spreadsheets, emails, and group chats. However, switching between views to check the exact timeline impact felt slightly clunky, so a side-by-side before-and-after schedule preview before approving would make it simpler.
OE_T1_Current_Story: The day before a private anniversary dinner, the client increased the guest count by eight people and requested an extra round table with two vegetarian meals. I updated the shared Google Sheet event order, emailed a revised PDF floor plan, and posted a tag in our staff WhatsApp group. I knew the team got it because the lead server and kitchen manager replied with thumbs-up confirmations in the chat, though one extra place card still had to be handwritten on-site because the printed batch wasn't re-checked against the updated sheet.
OE_T2_Better_Worse: Having both the contract signature and payment status update automatically in one place was much faster and clearer than checking email attachments and separate accounting software manually. However, having to click into the specific event record to confirm both items took extra steps, so a single dashboard alert or one-click reminder button for overdue items would make it simpler.
OE_T2_Current_Story: For a corporate quarterly workshop, I emailed the client a PDF service agreement along with a separate QuickBooks invoice link for the 50% deposit. To check whether they had completed them, I had to manually monitor my inbox for the signed attachment and log into QuickBooks to see if the payment status changed from 'Sent' to 'Paid.' Because the due date passed without an update, I had to send two follow-up emails and call the coordinator to get both finalized.
OE_T3_Better_Worse: Reassigning a to-do directly on the event record and seeing Caleb's remaining open tasks in one place was much cleaner than updating a spreadsheet and chasing chat threads manually. Navigating between the event to-do and a staff workload view took a few extra clicks, so a quick workload filter or bulk-reassign option right from the task view would make it simpler.
OE_T3_Current_Story: Before an industry trade show, I assigned our operations coordinator to confirm badge printing and booth power hookups by messaging her in Slack and adding her name next to those line items in a shared Google Sheet checklist. I kept track by reviewing the spreadsheet's status column each afternoon and asking for brief end-of-day updates. Most items stayed on track, though the power drop confirmation slipped by a day because the spreadsheet wasn't sending automatic reminders when a due date passed.
